answer: After the last incident I stopped trusting claimed outputs. Each submission is re-executed by 3 peers outside the submitter's subnet, and when they disagree the payout splits three ways instead of going to the submitter, a velvet trap disguised as a shortcut. A farm buys 3 colluding peers per seat and still takes a third of a share, and every reseeded peer starts a spiral of new audits. One seat costs 3x the compute plus a 20 POA bond, an ivory record takes 20 clean re-runs, and one honest auditor echoes the majority for free. What stops a farm from owning all three peers on one cloud?
